## What I implemented

- **`Version.__str__`** — canonical `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease][+build]`.
- **`parse`** — strict SemVer 2.0.0 parsing with:
  - ASCII-only identifiers,
  - non-empty dot-separated identifiers,
  - no leading zeros in core numbers or all-numeric pre-release identifiers,
  - build identifiers allowed to have leading zeros,
  - build metadata preserved but ignored for precedence.
- **`compare`** — accepts `str` or `Version`; compares core numerically, applies pre-release rules (numeric vs alphanumeric, ASCII ordering, shorter-list rule), ignores build metadata.
- **`satisfies`** — parses `||`-joined comparator sets, whitespace-separated comparators, operators `=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `^`, `~`, including the pre-release gating rule per comparator set. Invalid versions/ranges raise `ValueError`.

## Design decisions

- Used a compiled regex for strict structural validation, with a separate explicit check for leading zeros in numeric pre-release identifiers.
- Comparator operators are parsed by longest prefix (`>=`, `<=`, then single-character operators), so no space is allowed between an operator and its version, matching “prefixed by an operator.”
- `^0.0.0` uses the conventional upper bound `<0.0.1` since there is no leftmost non-zero part.
- Numeric pre-release identifiers are compared by normalized length then lexicographically, avoiding integer conversion of arbitrarily long identifiers.
- Core numeric parts are built in 9-digit chunks, avoiding Python 3.11+’s decimal-string-to-int length limit.
- Equality in ranges is equality of precedence, so build metadata differences do not affect matching.
